pages.text: Dark clouds rolled over the neighborhood as the first drops of rain began to fall. <name> spotted Mom’s umbrella lying forgotten on the porch. “I have to save it before the rain gets heavy!” he shouted, hopping onto his bright blue cycle.

Pedaling fast, <name> raced down the lane, dodging puddles that splashed like tiny fountains. Each puddle was a new challenge — he laughed as his tires skidded slightly, sending water flying onto the walls and bushes.

The wind gusted, pushing him forward, and <name> leaned into it, pretending he was flying. Around the corner, a stray leaf blew across his path, but quick reflexes helped him swerve safely. He rang his bell as he passed neighbors, shouting, “Umbrella coming through!”

A big puddle stretched across the street. <name> took a running start, pedaling furiously, and splashed right through, laughing as water sprayed high. His shirt was wet, his shoes squishy, but he didn’t slow down. The rain felt like a cheering crowd, urging him onward.
Finally, he reached the porch and handed the umbrella to his mother, puffing from excitement. “Saved it just in time!” he said proudly.

Mom smiled and opened the umbrella, but then laughed, “Why don’t we enjoy the rain together?” <name> hopped back on his cycle, splashing through puddles with Mom and little sister beside him. They laughed, raced, and danced in the rain, celebrating a mission accomplished and a joyful monsoon afternoon.
